evidence: Ch. 4 sidebar table row: "Self-host — 21-host peak KV-screen fleet ... $155,816.93 ... 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.33 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16)"

fix_instruction: Extend the Preface's cross-reference rule to cover three-level references (Chapter N, Section M, Subsection P) and state that top-level spine sections are numbered within the chapter (Concept=§1, Mental Model=§2, Worked Example=§3, Measurement=§4, Common Mistakes=§5, Architecture Consequence=§6).

evidence: Ch. 1 §1.1.4: "~1 FLOP/byte for full MHA at FP16 (4·n_layers·L·d FLOPs against 4·n_layers·L·d bytes, two matmuls at two FLOPs each over two FP16 tensors at two bytes each), far below the H100 roofline ridge of ~295 FLOP/byte (Ch. 2, Ch. 8)."
issue: Arithmetic/notation defect: the FLOP count 4·n_layers·L·d and the byte count 4·n_layers·L·d are written identically, so the ratio as printed is 1 FLOP/byte only because the two are equal by construction — but the byte count omits the factor-of-2 for two tensors and is derived as (2 tensors × 2 B × n_layers × L × d) = 4·n_layers·L·d while the FLOP count as written (2 matmuls × 2 FLOPs × n_layers × L × d) = 4·n_layers·L·d. The two derivations happen to coincide, so the reader cannot tell which of the two different factorizations is intended, and the FLOP expression omits the head/KV-width detail that the bytes expression implies. The book's own decode-intensity figure elsewhere (Ch. 6, p. 118) uses 4·L·d_model·n_layers ≈ 24.1 GFLOP against 24.1 GB — the same identity, so this is a presentation ambiguity rather than a numeric error, but the two expressions are written so that they look like a typo.
fix_instruction: Write the two terms with their separate factorizations: FLOPs = 2 matmuls × 2 FLOP × n_layers × L × d_head·n_heads, and bytes = 2 tensors × 2 B × n_layers × L × d_head·n_KV, and state explicitly that for full MHA d_head·n_heads = d_head·n_KV = d, which is why the two reduce to the same expression and the intensity is ~1 FLOP/byte.

evidence: Ch. 6 §6.3.1: "The two-point analytic mean is 0.842 s (0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0; the display above rounds it to 0.84 s). The plotted synthetic stream's exact mean is 0.85 s — the value Fig 6.2 displays."
issue: Arithmetic defect: 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 = 0.792 + 0.05 = 0.842 s. But the population mixture as described (99% log-normal with median 0.8 s and σ ≈ 0.12, 1% at 5.0 s) has an analytic mean of 0.99 × E[log-normal] + 0.01 × 5.0, where E[log-normal] = exp(μ + σ²/2) = 0.8 × exp(0.0072) ≈ 0.8058, giving ≈ 0.8476 s — not 0.842 s. The book's '0.842 s' is the two-point approximation (treating the log-normal as its median), yet it is labelled 'the two-point analytic mean' while being presented alongside 'the plotted synthetic stream's exact mean is 0.85 s' as if they were both analytic quantities; the 0.85 s sample value is a single draw of N = 10,000 and is draw-dependent exactly as the p99 is later shown to be (p. 99 at 100 stragglers vs 101).
fix_instruction: State three distinct quantities: (a) the two-point median-substitution approximation 0.842 s; (b) the analytic mixture mean 0.99 × 0.8·exp(σ²/2) + 0.05 ≈ 0.848 s; (c) the sample mean of this particular draw ≈ 0.85 s, with the same draw-dependence caveat the p99 receives.

evidence: Ch. 6 §6.3.2: "Scenario A [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]: the extra 20 tok/s are produced, but they land in the tail that misses the SLO, so goodput does not grow — goodput is unchanged only at f ≈ 68.6 % (48 ÷ 70)..." and later "the compliant fraction falls from 96% to 94%, goodput is 50×0.96 = 48 vs 70×0.94 = 65.8"
issue: Internal contradiction / prose defect: the paragraph first asserts as its Scenario A conclusion that 'goodput does not grow' and 'goodput is unchanged only at f ≈ 68.6%', then immediately presents Scenario B where goodput rises from 48 to 65.8. The Scenario A framing ('the extra 20 tok/s are produced, but they land in the tail that misses the SLO') is asserted rather than derived, and the derived f ≈ 68.6% contradicts the 94% case in the very next sentence — the text then acknowledges this ('The case the opening claim describes is the third one'), but the opening sentence is left standing as a claim in its own right.
fix_instruction: Restructure the three scenarios so each is introduced with its own f and outcome (f = 68.6% → unchanged; f = 94% → rises; f = 65% → falls) and remove the unqualified opening sentence 'goodput does not grow', replacing it with a pointer to the f that produces it.

evidence: Ch. 6 §6.8: "the peak demands ~18.6× one host's prefill capacity... Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21... the peak prefill oversubscription falls from 18.6× to 51.6 ÷ (21 × 2.77) ≈ 0.9×"
issue: Arithmetic check that does not close cleanly: 51.6 PFLOP/s ÷ (21 hosts × 2.77 PFLOP/s per host) = 51.6 ÷ 58.17 = 0.887 ≈ 0.89, printed as '≈ 0.9×'. The rounding is loose but acceptable; the harder issue is the internal consistency of the per-host sustained capacity: Ch. 8's per-host figure of ~2.77 PFLOP/s comes from 8 × 0.989 PFLOPS × 0.35 = 2.769 PFLOP/s, while Ch. 8's token-rate version of the same capacity is ~19,780 tok/s ÷ 140 GFLOP/token = 2.769 PFLOP/s — consistent. However the mini-case elsewhere (p. 124) states 10 rps '≈ 4.7 host-equivalents' (12.9 ÷ 2.77 = 4.66) and the peak 18.6 (51.6 ÷ 2.77 = 18.63), so the ratios are consistent but the '0.9×' residual is presented without the '≥' / upper-bound qualifier that the same paragraph applies to the 16.2 host-equivalent residual figure ('bound-derived, not measured').
fix_instruction: Carry the same qualifier onto the post-scale figure: print '≈0.89× (an upper bound on the post-cache ratio, before any prefix-cache saving)', so the two residual figures (16.2 host-equivalents and 0.9×) share one status statement.

evidence: Ch. 4 §4.8: "A prefill-throughput cross-check from the Chapter 8 model bounds it from below: 50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host... ≈ ~24 hosts (460,000 ÷ 19,800 = 23.23, ceiled to a whole host)."
issue: Rounding/label defect: 23.23 ceiled is 24, which the text states, but the sentence's leading phrase 'bounds it from below' is misleading — a prefill screen of 24 hosts is 2 hosts below the binding KV screen of 26, so it is a weaker lower bound, and the text later says 'the binding figure is the KV-residency/service-time ~26'. The phrase 'bounds it from below' is technically about the fleet size (24 ≤ 26 ≤ 40) but sits immediately after '≈ ~24 hosts' with a doubled approximation marker ('≈ ~'), a typographic duplication that recurs in the chapter (e.g. '~21 hosts (⌈344/17⌉ = 21)' is fine, but '26 (full util) / ~38 ... 39 before the spare' mixes bare and tilde forms for the same quantity).
fix_instruction: Remove the doubled '≈ ~' and harmonize the approximation markers for the same derived quantity within the paragraph and mini-case; restate the cross-check as 'a weaker lower bound (24 hosts) than the binding KV screen (26 hosts)'.

evidence: Ch. 3 §3.1.1 and Fig. 3.2 caption: "Full-canvas masked sampler: accept selected IDs ... Full bidirectional forwards: fixed IDs can still acquire new K/V." C ?' — i.e. accepted IDs out of order with the prompt held fixed — while the caption states accepted IDs 'become fixed resolved positions'.
